title: Whether to set up a council on Integrated Shield Plan and rider premium increases
asked: Mr Yip Hon Weng asked whether the Ministry will consider establishing a council to provide recommendations on reasonable Integrated Shield Plan and rider premium increases for private healthcare.
response: Ms Rahayu Mahzam said Integrated Shield Plans and riders are private, commercial products in a competitive market, so the size and frequency of premium revisions are left to insurers' actuarial and commercial considerations and market forces. She said the Government's role is to ensure affordable, accessible and good quality subsidised healthcare. She added that information and guidelines are available to help consumers, and that the Ministry is looking at approaches including benchmarks for private professional fees, has taken enforcement action against a small minority of doctors with errant claims, and has intervened to improve consumer fairness and transparency.

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and riders are private, commercial products and IP insurers operate in a competitive market.

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: the quantum and frequency of premium revisions are subject to insurers' actuarial and commercial considerations which are best left to market forces.

key_points.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
key_points.quote: The Government's role should be to ensure affordable, accessible and good quality subsidised healthcare for Singaporeans.

key_points.quote: we do have to leave some of this to market forces
